title: "Getting Started"
---

::: {.callout-warning}
**Preview install.** Use the source checkout for the current review build. A
package-index release has not been published, and the MLPerf EDU component
license remains a release gate.
:::

This guide takes you from an empty checkout to a functional dashboard and one
quality-bearing result. A GPU is optional. PyTorch uses Apple MPS or CUDA when
available and otherwise runs the supported path on CPU.

## Before You Begin

Use macOS, Linux, or a Linux environment such as WSL. The commands on this site
use a POSIX-compatible shell. Confirm that Git and
[uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) are available.

```bash
git --version
uv --version
```

MLPerf EDU supports Python 3.10 or newer. `uv` selects and manages the locked
project environment, so a separate virtual-environment command is not needed.

## Run the Guided Setup

```bash
git clone https://github.com/harvard-edge/cs249r_book
cd cs249r_book/mlperf-edu
uv sync --locked
uv run mlperf init --profile min --output-dir submissions/first-run
```

`init` performs the shortest complete product journey. It checks Python,
PyTorch, the available device, caches, and the registry. It then runs the
four-workload starter collection, verifies every provenance manifest, and
writes aggregate HTML, JSON, and CSV reports. Nothing opens automatically.

The output directory should contain an aggregate suite report and four sets of
workload artifacts.

```text
submissions/first-run/
├── mlperf_edu_min_<timestamp>.html
├── mlperf_edu_min_<timestamp>.json
├── mlperf_edu_min_<timestamp>.csv
├── image-classification_min_report.*
├── causal-language-modeling_training_min_report.*
├── graph-node-classification_min_report.*
├── time-series-forecasting_min_report.*
└── *.provd.json
```

The terminal prints the exact report paths. Open the generated HTML file
directly when you want to inspect it. Routine setup and validation never open a
browser automatically.

## Understand the Three Setup Commands

| **Command** | **What It Does** | **When to Use It** |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `mlperf doctor` | Inspects the environment and selected workload prerequisites without running a benchmark | Diagnose setup or preflight a specific workload |
| `mlperf init` | Runs `doctor`, the four-workload starter smoke path, provenance verification, and reporting | First contact with the project |
| `mlperf health` | Runs and verifies all fourteen functional `min` paths and writes a suite health dashboard | Validate a course image or the full local installation |

Do not run all three during initial setup. `init` is the canonical first step.
Use `doctor` when something fails and `health` when you need complete functional
coverage.

## Read the First Dashboard

The `min` dashboard answers whether the selected paths executed and whether
their manifests verified. It does not compare functional diagnostics with
quality targets. Read the report in this order.

1. Confirm that every selected path executed.
2. Confirm that provenance verification passed.
3. Check the actual device and configuration used.
4. Treat secondary metrics as diagnostics, not benchmark scores.

The [results guide](guide/results.qmd) explains every dashboard state and the
claims each state supports.

## Run the First Quality Contract

Image classification is the recommended first `max` workload because it has a
small, bounded accuracy set and a direct target. Preview the contract and asset
work before downloading or measuring.

```bash
uv run mlperf show image-classification
uv run mlperf fetch --workload image-classification --profile max --dry-run
uv run mlperf fetch --workload image-classification --profile max
uv run mlperf run --workload image-classification --profile max \
  --output-dir submissions/image-max
```

The run writes HTML, JSON, CSV, and `.provd.json` files without opening them.
The HTML lead card reports top-1 accuracy, the target of at least 0.85, and the
pass or miss decision. Verify the recorded bytes after the run.

```bash
uv run mlperf verify submissions/image-max/image-classification_max.provd.json
```

## Know What Success Means

Execution success, provenance verification, and target attainment are separate
states. A valid run may miss its quality target. That is a scientific result,
not an execution failure. A missing dataset, crashed runner, or invalid
manifest is an execution problem and does not support a quality conclusion.

Continue with the [running guide](guide/running.qmd) for selection and profiles,
the [results guide](guide/results.qmd) for interpretation, or
[troubleshooting](guide/troubleshooting.qmd) if setup did not complete.

## Contributor Setup

The development tools are not required for normal benchmark use. Contributors
can install them after the student journey works.

```bash
uv sync --locked --extra dev
uv run python -m pytest
```
